area: Spike S2: the BlockOnPossibleDataLoss check forms and the Facsimile vocabulary's statement shapes on DacFx 162.5.57 and 170.5.96 (V3_MILESTONES.md:424; Facsimile ARCHITECTURE.md §11 question 3)
summary: Nothing for S2 is in the repository yet. Today one fixture fact covers this ground, on 170.5.96 only, for make-mandatory only: tests/Io.Tests/SpikeTests.cs:51-63 (Fact_3), using the visitor at SpikeTests.cs:157-169. tests/Golden/data-loss-checks/ does not exist. io/ pins DacFx to 170.5.96 for every project (Directory.Packages.props:2 and :9; locked restore at Directory.Build.props:15-16; ci/packages.allow:8). I ran the experiment in the scratch folder (about 15 minutes). DacFx 162.5.57 restores into a net10.0 project and runs under .NET 10.0.13: NuGet picks its lib/net8.0. Its whole dependency graph passes NuGet audit, which runs in mode all with warnings as errors (170's graph does not, without the Pkcs pin). A VersionOverride="162.5.57" restores cleanly under the repository's own Directory.Packages.props and Directory.Build.props, with a 291-line lock file. On dbchange-sql, both releases planned 38 golden heads three ways each: live Script, package-to-package, and against an extracted package. The result: one check form, `IF EXISTS (select top 1 1 from [s].[T])` then `RAISERROR (N'Rows were detected. The schema update is terminating because data loss might occur.', 16, 127) WITH NOWAIT`. It is byte-identical across both releases and all three modes. There is one check per table, above a /* */ comment that names each site on it. DacFx writes these lines with CRLF line endings. ScriptDom 180.102.0 (TSql160Parser) parsed every script from both releases without an error. After regeneration, the statements are the same on both releases for every head. The raw text differs only in the alignment whitespace of the boilerplate `VALUES (1)` line.

items.name: Run DacFx 162.5.57 beside the committed DacFx: a console project, tests/DacFx162/, that the fixture tests start as a child process
items.evidence: Central pin: Directory.Packages.props:9. The comment 'One version per package' is at Directory.Packages.props:2, and CentralPackageTransitivePinningEnabled=false is at :5. Lock files and CI locked mode: Directory.Build.props:15-16. The PackagesAllowlist test reads only PackageReference/PackageVersion ids (tests/Budgets.Tests/PackagesAllowlist.cs:24-37), and Microsoft.SqlServer.DacFx is already allowed (ci/packages.allow:8). There is precedent for a second process: Io.Tests runs itself as a dbchange process (tests/Io.Tests/Io.Tests.csproj:10-11), and test programs run through io/Command (tests/Budgets.Tests/Programs.cs:19-29). Measured in the scratch folder: the nuspec has net462, net6.0, net8.0 and netstandard2.1 groups; a net10.0 project resolves net8.0. It pulls SqlClient 5.1.6, ScriptDom 161.9142.1, Microsoft.Build 15.9.20 and Azure.Identity 1.11.4 (37 packages in all). Audit (NuGetAuditMode=all, level low) is clean. A VersionOverride under the root CPM restores with no NU warning. Under runtime 10.0.13 it ran Publish (12.0 s for the base), Script, the static Script(DacPackage, DacPackage, string, PublishOptions) and Extract(Stream, …) against SQL Server 2022 on 127.0.0.1,11434. The probe code is in the scratch folder: Plan.cs and tool162/tool162.csproj under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-outsystems-ddl-exporter/17755096-5809-5c10-a22d-d46e8371455a/scratchpad/scout/s2/. Routes I rejected: (1) Placing the project under tests/Golden/ to reuse its stop files (tests/Golden/Directory.Packages.props). It escapes warnings-as-errors and lock files. Its .cs and its ~290-line lock file would count against the 3,000-line golden data budget (ci/budgets.json 'golden') instead of the tests code budget. TestTraits.cs:44 skips tests/Golden/, so its tests would be invisible to ParityResolves. Those stop files exist for .sqlproj projects. (2) Loading 162 into an AssemblyLoadContext inside Io.Tests: Dac.dll and SqlClient would be loaded twice at different versions, and the dependency resolution is fragile. (3) The sqlpackage 162.5.57 dotnet tool: it would be a new supply-chain artifact (a tool manifest), it needs a .NET 8 runtime or roll-forward, and it is the same engine.
items.remaining: Create tests/DacFx162/DacFx162.csproj: Sdk Microsoft.NET.Sdk; OutputType Exe; AssemblyName DbChange.DacFx162; RootNamespace DbChange.DacFx162; ImplicitUsings disable; InvariantGlobalization false (SqlClient refuses invariant mode, as in Io.Tests.csproj:8-9); one item, <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.SqlServer.DacFx" VersionOverride="162.5.57" />. Reference no project, and let no project reference this one: a ProjectReference would flow DacFx 162 into the referrer's graph. Generate tests/DacFx162/packages.lock.json with a plain `dotnet restore` (the lock is required by PackagesAllowlist.cs:42-55). Add the project to DbChange.sln under the 'tests' solution folder (`dotnet sln DbChange.sln add tests/DacFx162/DacFx162.csproj --solution-folder tests`), so every CI job restores and builds it (dbchange.yml:36, :73, :99, :125). `dotnet test` skips it, as it already skips io, cli and kernel. Write tests/DacFx162/Program.cs (~70 lines, house style: braces, the CA1304/1305/1307/1309 culture rules, no implicit usings): `static int Main(string[] args)`. First Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable("DACFX_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT", "1"). Then print `DacFx <major.minor.build>` from FileVersionInfo of typeof(DacServices).Assembly.Location, as io/DacFx.cs:47-48 and :91-93 read it. One verb: `script <profile.xml> <database> <out folder> <name>=<dacpac>...`. Take the connection from the environment variable DBCHANGE_DACFX162_CONNECTION, never from argv, because io/Command prints its arguments. options = DacProfile.Load(profile).DeployOptions. For each head: open a FileStream and call DacPackage.Load(stream); loading by path loads SampleCatalog.dll beside it (GoldenProject.Io.cs:48-50). Then `new DacServices(connection).Script(package, database, new PublishOptions { GenerateDeploymentScript = true, GenerateDeploymentReport = false, DeployOptions = options }).DatabaseScript`, written UTF-8 without a BOM to <out>/<name>.sql. Return exit 0. On any exception, write e.Message to stderr and return exit 1. Leave room for the S9 and S10 scouts to add their verbs (extract, publish) to the same program.

items.name: The extracted checks under tests/Golden/data-loss-checks/, and the fixture test that pins both releases to them
items.evidence: V3_MILESTONES.md:424 (S2: 'the extracted checks only'); :1162-1163 and ci/budgets.json 'golden' (ceiling 3,000; 1,461 lines today by git ls-files | wc). The extraction shape already exists at SpikeTests.cs:157-169: an IfStatement whose Predicate is an ExistsPredicate and whose ThenStatement is a RaiseErrorStatement with ThirdParameter IntegerLiteral "127". The script is read with SQLCMD ':' lines dropped (SpikeTests.cs:55-56). Measured: 11 of the 38 heads write checks. Each check is 2 lines; together they are 24 lines, staged at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-outsystems-ddl-exporter/17755096-5809-5c10-a22d-d46e8371455a/scratchpad/scout/s2/proposed/data-loss-checks/*.sql. They were identical in 162-live, 170-live, 162-package, 170-package, 162-extracted and 170-extracted. The checks do not depend on the data: the package-to-package plans have no rows and agree with the live plans against the seeded copy (Customer 5, Product 5, Category 3 rows). Placement, the same on both releases: the inlined pre-deploy script runs first; then each table's check in its own batch, under a /* */ comment naming each site on that table; then the transaction. For example, make-mandatory's script has the pre-deploy at line 133, the check at 142 and BEGIN TRANSACTION at 154.
items.remaining:
File format: tests/Golden/data-loss-checks/<sample change>.sql, LF, UTF-8 without a BOM, ending with a newline. It holds only the check statements, in script order. Each is the IfStatement's text exactly as DacFx wrote it, taken from the token range [StartOffset, StartOffset+FragmentLength) of the parsed script, with 
 turned into 
 and a 
 after each. No comment, no GO, no header. If a release ever writes a check differently, add <sample change>.<release>.sql (for example make-mandatory.162.5.57.sql); that release reads it in place of the shared file. None is needed today. A sample change with no file is the claim that it writes no check, and the test enforces that claim.

In tests/Io.Tests/DataLossCheckTests.cs (~250 lines), write a class fixture `PlannedOnBothDacFxReleases : IAsyncLifetime`. Use [Collection(PublishedToolCollection.Name)] or construct PublishedTool as GoldenProject does. It: (1) builds the base and every GoldenProject.SampleChanges head with Task.WhenAll(GoldenProject.Built(change)); (2) makes one copy with SqlServerFixture.RegisterAsync() and runs GoldenProject.Publish(base, copy, GoldenProject.Pipeline()), which seeds it through the post-deploy script; (3) gets the 170.5.96 live script per head as PublishedGoldenProject.Plan does (SpikeTests.cs:216-226), but against copy.ConnectionString; (4) gets the 170.5.96 package script per head through io's own plan, DacFx.Plan(Ssdt.Open(head), Ssdt.Open(base), copy.Name, <Strict profile>, []).Script, the path predict will read (io/DacFx.cs:122); (5) gets the 162.5.57 live scripts with one child process, `new Command("dotnet", [<repo>/tests/DacFx162/bin/<cfg>/net10.0/DbChange.DacFx162.dll, "script", GoldenProject.Profile, copy.Name, <scratch>, name=path…], Programs.Default) { Directory = Repository.Root, Environment = { DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1, DACFX_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1, DBCHANGE_DACFX162_CONNECTION=copy.ConnectionString } }.Finish()`, with <cfg> taken from AppContext.BaseDirectory's parent folder names; it asserts exit 0 and a first line of `DacFx 162.5.57`; (6) normalizes every script's CRLF to LF and keeps them in memory, with the full scripts kept only in a ScratchFolder and never committed. Move SpikeTests' private BlockOnPossibleDataLossChecks visitor into one internal `DataLossChecks.In(string script) -> IReadOnlyList<string>` (the verbatim LF texts) and use it from SpikeTests too. The fixture Theory, over every sample change name, compares the three scripts' DataLossChecks.In against the committed file (the release-specific one when present). Write each expected file from the 170 live extraction. They should equal the staged proposed/data-loss-checks files: add-mandatory-no-default, cut-scale, drop-a-column, drop-a-column-and-narrow-another, make-mandatory, narrow-a-column, narrow-precision, rename-a-column-without-the-refactorlog, retype-int-to-smallint, retype-nvarchar-to-int, two-sites-on-one-table. items.name: The vocabulary's receipts: Facsimile ARCHITECTURE.md §11 question 3, and its §4 shapes on both releases
items.evidence: The vocabulary table is at archive/v2/ssdt-agent/facsimile/ARCHITECTURE.md:164-205 and the question at :528. The verify cases that wait on it: cases/10-questions.md:298-308 (QST-15, the guard spelled without WITH NOWAIT), cases/40-ops-columns.md:555-567 (OP-widen-03, whether the data-loss comment names every lossy ALTER COLUMN and never a widening), and cases/41-ops-keys.md:1249-1266 (OP-toggle-trust-05, the re-enable statements; S9's). WP 2.1 (V3_MILESTONES.md:520) matches KeyLength, Rebuild, Computed, Temporal, Scan, Authored and SeedDrift on io/TSql's typed statements; io/TSql.cs:16-53 is the parser and generator. Measured on both releases (the statement lists match after Sql160ScriptGenerator regeneration, for all 38 heads in every mode): HasRows holds, with WITH NOWAIT on both, so QST-15's no-NOWAIT spelling appears on neither. NotNull holds: `ALTER TABLE [dbo].[Customer] ALTER COLUMN [Email] NVARCHAR (256) NOT NULL`. Fits holds for length, precision, scale and type, and DacFx drops and re-adds a column's DEFAULT around the ALTER (DROP CONSTRAINT [DF_Order_Total] … ADD CONSTRAINT [DF_Order_Total] DEFAULT (0) FOR [Total]); this also happens for make-optional. A collation change writes `ALTER COLUMN [Name] NVARCHAR (100) COLLATE Latin1_General_CS_AS NOT NULL` with no guard and no comment. OP-widen-03 is answered yes: the comment names every narrowing measured ('The type for column Code in table [dbo].[Product] is currently  NVARCHAR (50) NOT NULL but is being changed to  NVARCHAR (10) NOT NULL. Data loss could occur…'), the NOT NULL tightening, the NOT NULL add without a default and each drop; it never names a widening or a collation change. The comments are identical on both releases. Unique holds: `CREATE UNIQUE NONCLUSTERED INDEX [UIX_Product_Code] ON [dbo].[Product]([Code] ASC)`, an optional WHERE, and `ADD CONSTRAINT [UQ_Product_Code] UNIQUE NONCLUSTERED ([Code] ASC)`. A clustered primary key change, however, is a rebuild: the key sits inside `CREATE TABLE [dbo].[tmp_ms_xx_OrderLine] (… CONSTRAINT [tmp_ms_xx_constraint_PK_OrderLine1] PRIMARY KEY CLUSTERED …)` followed by sp_rename, not an ADD CONSTRAINT. Orphan and CheckFalse hold for named constraints (`WITH NOCHECK ADD CONSTRAINT [x] …` then `WITH CHECK CHECK CONSTRAINT [x]`). They do not hold for unnamed ones: DacFx writes `WITH NOCHECK ADD FOREIGN KEY|CHECK (…)` and validates through a cursor over sys.objects, running a built `ALTER TABLE … WITH CHECK CHECK CONSTRAINT` with sp_executesql, then `RAISERROR (N'An error occurred while verifying constraints', 16, 127)` if any failed. This is the same on both releases, on a new table and on a populated one. KeyLength: a plain `CREATE NONCLUSTERED INDEX [IX_Product_Name] ON [dbo].[Product]([Name] ASC)`; the over-limit key appears nowhere in the script. Rebuild holds: `CREATE TABLE [dbo].[tmp_ms_xx_T]`, then `INSERT INTO … SELECT … FROM [dbo].[T] ORDER BY …`, wrapped in `IF EXISTS (SELECT TOP 1 1 FROM [dbo].[T]) BEGIN SET IDENTITY_INSERT … END` when the table has an identity, then DROP TABLE and two sp_renames. Computed holds: `ADD [CodeLength] AS LEN(Code) PERSISTED`. Temporal holds, but on [dbo].[tmp_ms_xx_Account] inside a rebuild: `ADD PERIOD FOR SYSTEM_TIME ([ValidFrom], [ValidTo])` and `SET (SYSTEM_VERSIONING = ON (HISTORY_TABLE=[dbo].[AccountHistory], DATA_CONSISTENCY_CHECK=ON))`. Scan holds for a non-unique CREATE INDEX and a widening ALTER COLUMN. A defaulted NOT NULL add is spelled `ADD [Tier] INT CONSTRAINT [DF_Customer_Tier] DEFAULT (0) NOT NULL`, with DEFAULT before NOT NULL. Authored: the pre-deploy and post-deploy text is inlined verbatim. Mode, not release: a live Script adds `WAITFOR DELAY '00:00.010'` batches that package-to-package plans lack.
items.remaining: In DataLossCheckTests.cs, two more fixture tests over PlannedOnBothDacFxReleases. (a) Theory over sample changes: Both DacFx releases plan each sample change as the same statements. Compare live with live only, because of the WAITFOR batches. (b) Theory with InlineData receipts (kind, sample change, ScriptDom statement type, fragment of the regenerated text), asserting each row in both releases' live scripts. risks: A constraint-verification failure is indistinguishable by number from a data-loss block. DacFx validates an unnamed FOREIGN KEY or CHECK through a cursor and, if any fail, raises RAISERROR (N'An error occurred while verifying constraints', 16, 127). That is Msg 50000 at state 127, the same number and state as the BlockOnPossibleDataLoss check. io classifies a block by the quoted number (kernel/DacFxMessage.cs:18, io/DacFx.cs:248), so WP 4.1's blockedBy could report a failed unnamed-constraint validation as block-on-possible-data-loss. It must tell them apart by the message text.

State 127 is not unique, and IF EXISTS (SELECT TOP 1 1 FROM T) is not unique either: the rebuild's copy step uses the same predicate with a BEGIN…INSERT…END body. Every golden script also carries the guard's text inside the pre-deploy block comment (make-mandatory's script, line 73). A reader that searches text instead of parsing will over-count.

Bandwidth: restoring DacFx 162.5.57 adds 37 packages (~314 MB unpacked for DacFx alone) to every job's restore, because the project is in the solution. Nothing caches NuGet on these runners today.

The 162 graph passes NuGet audit today: Microsoft.Build 15.9.20, Azure.Identity 1.11.4, Microsoft.Data.SqlClient 5.1.6, Microsoft.IdentityModel 6.35.0. A future advisory turns that into NU1902/NU1903 errors in every job's locked restore. The remedy then is an explicit higher PackageReference in tests/DacFx162 alone, with a decision line, as the Pkcs pin was for io.

'Both releases' assumes 162.5.57 is the pipeline's release until S7 reads the Octopus step. If S7 names another release, the VersionOverride and the lock file move, and every assertion re-runs unchanged.

A stale tests/DacFx162 build could run old code, because the child is found by path under bin/<cfg>/net10.0. The test must assert the child's printed release and fail on a missing dll, naming the build to run.

The committed checks are DacFx's bytes with CRLF turned into LF (DacFx writes CRLF inside the script). A test that forgets the normalization fails on every platform, and .gitattributes forces the committed file to LF.

Live plans and package-to-package plans differ in WAITFOR DELAY '00:00.010' batches. Statement-shape comparisons must pair the same mode across releases; check comparisons may cross modes, since all six combinations agree.
This was measured on SQL Server 2022 in Docker (dbchange-sql). LocalDB 16.x and other compatibility levels were not measured; CI's Windows job will be the first run there.
